To resolve this dichotomy, we introduce the Independent Combinatorial Tokens (ICT) framework, which shifts the optimization focus from scalar uncertainty to the distributional properties of token logits. By leveraging the Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence between token logits distributions, ICT identifies tokens with distinctive distributional patterns as critical branching points for guiding effective exploration in LLM reasoning. Our theoretical analysis, grounded in both Shannon and second-order Rényi entropy, proves that selectively updating on these tokens regulates policy concentration: it reduces the overall distribution uncertainty measured by Shannon entropy, while controlling probability concentration captured by second-order Rényi entropy. This dual effect prevents over-concentrated token generation from weakening exploration and effectively stabilizes the training landscape. Empirical results demonstrate that updating only the top 10% of unique tokens on Qwen2.5 (0.5B/1.5B/7B) models yields an average pass@4 improvement of 4.58%, with a maximum gain of 14.9%, over GRPO, 20-Entropy, and STAPO baselines across seven benchmarks spanning math, commonsense, and Olympiad-level problems.

AI.tldr: RLVR suffers from entropy collapse or explosion. The ICT framework resolves this by selectively updating tokens based on JS divergence of logit distributions, using only top 10% unique tokens, yielding 4.58% avg pass@4 improvement over baselines across math and reasoning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: RLVR faces a fundamental optimization instability: uniform token updates cause entropy collapse (premature convergence to suboptimal strategies) while excessive entropy maximization causes entropy explosion (blind exploration toward incoherent reasoning chains).
AI.method: ICT shifts optimization from scalar uncertainty to distributional properties of token logits, using JS divergence between token logit distributions to identify critical branching points, with selective updates grounded in Shannon and second-order Rényi entropy analysis.
AI.result: Updating only top 10% unique tokens on Qwen2.5 (0.5B/1.5B/7B) yields average 4.58% pass@4 improvement (max 14.9%) over GRPO, 20-Entropy, and STAPO baselines across seven benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Selective token updating via distributional analysis prevents over-concentrated generation and stabilizes training, effectively resolving the entropy collapse-explosion dichotomy in RLVR.

title: World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving
summary: Autonomous vehicles must operate safely in the real world, where errors can have severe consequences. Although modern end-to-end driving policies excel in routine scenarios, their reliability is limited by the scarcity of safety-critical ``long-tail'' events in real driving datasets. These rare interactions define the practical safety boundary of the learned policy, yet they are difficult to collect at scale in the real world. Here we show that this fundamental limitation can be addressed by post-training pre-trained driving models on synthesized high-stakes interactions. We introduce World Engine, a generative framework that reconstructs high-fidelity interactive environments from real-world logs and systematically extrapolates them into realistic safety-critical variations. This paradigm enables reinforcement-based post-training to align policies with safety constraints, circumventing the physical risks inherent in real-world exploration. On a public benchmark built on nuPlan, World Engine substantially reduces failures in rare safety-critical scenarios and yields significantly larger gains than scaling pre-training data alone. Furthermore, when deployed on a production-scale autonomous driving system, the resulting policy reduces simulated collisions and demonstrates measurable improvements in on-road testing, showing that post-training on synthesized, safety-critical interactions offers a scalable and effective pathway to safer autonomous driving. The full codebase suite, including training, is released to the public.

AI.tldr: World Engine is a generative framework that reconstructs high-fidelity interactive driving environments from real-world logs and synthesizes safety-critical scenarios for post-training pre-trained driving models. This approach substantially reduces failures in rare long-tail events, outperforms scaling pre-training data alone, and shows measurable improvements in both simulated and on-road testing for autonomous driving safety.
AI.motivation: Autonomous driving policies suffer from limited reliability in safety-critical "long-tail" events due to scarcity of such rare interactions in real-world datasets, making them difficult to collect at scale and posing physical risks for real-world exploration.
AI.method: World Engine uses a generative framework that (1) reconstructs high-fidelity interactive environments from real-world logs, (2) systematically extrapolates them into realistic safety-critical variations, and (3) applies reinforcement-based post-training to align pre-trained driving policies with safety constraints using synthesized interactions.
AI.result: On nuPlan benchmark, World Engine substantially reduces failures in rare safety-critical scenarios with significantly larger gains than scaling pre-training data alone. In production-scale autonomous driving systems, it reduces simulated collisions and shows measurable improvements in on-road testing.
AI.conclusion: Post-training on synthesized, safety-critical interactions offers a scalable and effective pathway to safer autonomous driving, circumventing physical risks of real-world exploration while addressing the long-tail data scarcity problem.

title: AgentFinVQA: A Deployable Multi-Agent Pipeline for Auditable Financial Chart QA
summary: Financial chart question answering in regulated settings demands more than accuracy: practitioners must know which answers to trust before acting on them, and many institutions cannot send client data to external model providers. Yet existing chart-QA agents are accuracy-focused and opaque, and most assume proprietary API access; to our knowledge, none combines auditability with on-premise deployability without significant accuracy compromise. We present AgentFinVQA, a multi-agent pipeline that decomposes each query into planning, OCR, legend grounding, visual inspection, and verification, recording every step in a traceable Model Evaluation Packet (MEP) per sample. On FinMME, AgentFinVQA improves $+7.68$ pp over a primary-backbone matched zero-shot baseline with a proprietary backbone (Gemini-3 Flash; 71.24% vs. 63.56%, McNemar $p \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-16}$), and $+4.84$ pp with open-weights Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 served locally. The verifier's verdict also serves as a useful confidence signal (68.2% vs. 55.6% exact accuracy on confirmed vs. revised answers), enabling human-in-the-loop review routing. Error analysis shows that question misunderstanding, legend confusion and extraction error account for nearly two-thirds of failures and are the categories least detected by the verifier, identifying clear directions for future work. Together these results show that auditable, on-premise financial chart QA is practical and that the open-weights system keeps most of the accuracy gains while enabling full data residency. We release our code to support reproducible evaluation.

AI.tldr: AgentFinVQA is a multi-agent pipeline for financial chart question answering that prioritizes auditability and on-premise deployment alongside accuracy. It uses a chain of specialized agents (planning, OCR, legend grounding, visual inspection, verification) and records traceable MEPs per sample. It improves accuracy by +7.68 pp over a zero-shot baseline with a proprietary backbone (Gemini-3 Flash) and +4.84 pp with open-weights Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 served locally. The verifier's confidence signal enables human-in-the-loop review. Error analysis reveals question misunderstanding, legend confusion, and extraction errors as primary failure modes.
AI.motivation: Existing financial chart-QA agents are accuracy-focused and opaque, and most assume proprietary API access. No existing system combines auditability with on-premise deployability without significant accuracy compromise, which is essential for regulated financial settings where trust and data privacy are critical.
AI.method: A multi-agent pipeline decomposing each query into five stages: planning, OCR, legend grounding, visual inspection, and verification. Each sample's processing steps are recorded in a traceable Model Evaluation Packet (MEP). The system supports both proprietary (Gemini-3 Flash) and open-weights (Qwen3.6-27B-FP8) backbones, enabling on-premise deployment.
AI.result: +7.68 pp improvement over zero-shot baseline on FinMME with Gemini-3 Flash (71.24% vs. 63.56%, McNemar p ≈ 1.1×10⁻¹⁶), +4.84 pp with open-weights Qwen3.6-27B-FP8. Verifier confidence signal yields 68.2% vs. 55.6% exact accuracy on confirmed vs. revised answers. Error analysis shows question misunderstanding, legend confusion, and extraction errors account for nearly two-thirds of failures.
AI.conclusion: Auditable, on-premise financial chart QA is practical. The open-weights system retains most accuracy gains while enabling full data residency. Clear directions for future work are identified from error analysis (question misunderstanding, legend confusion, extraction errors as undetected failure modes). Code is released for reproducibility.

title: MMD-SLAM: Structure-Enhanced Multi-Meta Gaussian Distribution-Guided Visual SLAM
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has significantly boosted novel view synthesis and high-fidelity scene reconstruction, expanding the potential of 3DGS-based Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) methods. However, most existing systems fail to fully exploit the underlying structural information, which limits rendering quality and often leads to inconsistent maps. To address these limitations, we propose MMD-SLAM, a structure-enhanced Visual SLAM framework that leverages the Atlanta World (AW) assumption to guide a Multi-Meta Gaussian representation for photorealistic mapping. First, we introduce a point-line fusion strategy for pose optimization, where 3D line segments are incorporated to improve tracking robustness and provide additional constraints for mapping. Second, we design a Multi-Meta Gaussian representation with dominant directions, explicitly encoding structural priors from the AW hypothesis. Finally, we propose a Gaussian evolution strategy that adapts to scene geometry and incorporates structural cues into global optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that these innovations enable MMD-SLAM to achieve state-of-the-art performance in both tracking accuracy and mapping quality. e.g., our method achieves a 48.56% reduction in ATE RMSE on ScanNet and a 5.71% improvement in PSNR on Replica, compared with MonoGS.

AI.tldr: MMD-SLAM is a structure-enhanced Visual SLAM framework using Atlanta World assumptions and Multi-Meta Gaussian representations to improve tracking accuracy and mapping quality, achieving 48.56% lower ATE RMSE on ScanNet and 5.71% higher PSNR on Replica vs. MonoGS.
AI.motivation: Existing 3DGS-based SLAM systems fail to fully exploit underlying structural information, limiting rendering quality and leading to inconsistent maps.
AI.method: (1) Point-line fusion strategy for pose optimization using 3D line segments; (2) Multi-Meta Gaussian representation with dominant directions encoding structural priors from Atlanta World assumption; (3) Gaussian evolution strategy adapting to scene geometry with structural cues for global optimization.
AI.result: State-of-the-art performance: 48.56% reduction in ATE RMSE on ScanNet, 5.71% improvement in PSNR on Replica compared to MonoGS.
AI.conclusion: The proposed structural enhancements enable superior tracking accuracy and photorealistic mapping quality in 3DGS-based Visual SLAM.

title: ORAgentBench: Can LLM Agents Solve Challenging Operations Research Tasks End to End?
summary: Large language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents for multi-step tasks in executable environments, yet their ability to perform realistic operations research (OR) work remains unclear. Existing OR evaluations often decouple modeling from solving, rely on pre-formalized or text-only instances, and rarely test the full workflow from operational artifacts to validated decisions. In this work, we introduce ORAgentBench, an execution-grounded benchmark for evaluating autonomous agents on challenging end-to-end operations research tasks. It contains 107 human-reviewed tasks across diverse operational scenarios, each packaged in an isolated environment with a natural-language brief, multi-file data, configuration artifacts, and a required submission schema. Agents must write and run solution code, and their submissions are evaluated by hidden validators for schema validity, hard-constraint feasibility, and normalized objective quality. Experiments with fourteen frontier agent-model configurations show that current agents remain far from reliable OR practice. The best agent passes only 35.51% of all tasks and 20.59% of hard tasks, and many feasible submissions still fall below the required quality threshold. Failure analysis further shows that errors are dominated by strategic weaknesses, including missed operational rules, brittle formulations, weak feasible-solution construction, and insufficient solution improvement. OR-specific procedural skills increase hard-task feasibility, but do not reliably improve solution quality or pass rate. These results suggest that progress in OR agents requires moving beyond plausible optimization code toward dependable, high-quality operational decision-making.

AI.tldr: ORAagentBench is an execution-grounded benchmark for evaluating autonomous LLM agents on end-to-end operations research tasks. Current frontier agents fail reliably, with the best achieving only 35.51% pass rate on all tasks and 20.59% on hard tasks, with failures dominated by strategic weaknesses like missed operational rules and brittle formulations.
AI.motivation: Existing OR evaluations focus on isolated modeling or solving steps, use pre-formalized or text-only instances, and fail to test the full workflow from operational artifacts to validated decisions. There is a need to assess whether LLM agents can perform realistic, end-to-end OR work in executable environments.
AI.method: The benchmark contains 107 human-reviewed tasks across diverse operational scenarios, each packaged in an isolated environment with a natural-language brief, multi-file data, configuration artifacts, and a required submission schema. Agents write and run solution code; submissions are evaluated by hidden validators for schema validity, hard-constraint feasibility, and normalized objective quality.
AI.result: Experiments with 14 frontier agent-model configurations show the best agent passes only 35.51% of all tasks and 20.59% of hard tasks. Many feasible submissions fall below the required quality threshold. Errors are dominated by strategic weaknesses (missed operational rules, brittle formulations, weak feasible-solution construction, insufficient improvement).
AI.conclusion: Progress in OR agents requires moving beyond plausible optimization code toward dependable, high-quality operational decision-making. OR-specific procedural skills improve hard-task feasibility but do not reliably improve solution quality or pass rate.

title: One-to-Two Acting: A Novel Framework for Single-arm Agent Action Expansion to Dual Arms
summary: Dual-arm manipulation can improve throughput via parallel execution, but collecting bimanual demonstrations for training is costly and difficult. We present ExS2D, a hierarchical action expansion framework that enables dual-arm manipulation from single-arm supervision. ExS2D first generates structured subtasks from textual instructions while explicitly capturing temporal precedence. It then grounds each subtask into executable actions through subtask-guided action mapping in observation. Finally, precedence-aware action allocation and synchronized planning are performed by a multimodal large language model driven coordinator to select collision-free dual-arm executions. Simulation experiments demonstrate that ExS2D reduces the average execution steps by 54.4% while maintaining a comparable success rate to a single-arm baseline. Real-robot experiments on four tasks further demonstrate the reliability of ExS2D for dual-arm execution under few-shot single-arm samples, while using zero bimanual demonstrations.

AI.tldr: ExS2D enables dual-arm manipulation using only single-arm supervision by hierarchically expanding actions from text instructions, reducing execution steps by 54.4% while maintaining comparable success rates, with zero bimanual demonstrations needed.
AI.motivation: Training dual-arm manipulation requires costly bimanual demonstrations, which are difficult to collect. The paper aims to enable efficient dual-arm execution using only single-arm supervision, eliminating the need for paired bimanual data.
AI.method: ExS2D uses a three-stage hierarchical framework: (1) structured subtask generation from text with explicit temporal precedence capture, (2) subtask-guided action mapping in observation space, and (3) precedence-aware action allocation and synchronized planning via a multimodal LLM-driven coordinator for collision-free dual-arm execution.
AI.result: Simulation experiments show a 54.4% reduction in average execution steps with success rate comparable to single-arm baselines. Real-robot experiments across four tasks confirm reliability under few-shot single-arm samples with zero bimanual demonstrations.
AI.conclusion: ExS2D is an effective hierarchical framework for transferring single-arm supervision to dual-arm manipulation, achieving efficiency gains without requiring costly bimanual demonstration data.

title: CombEval: A Framework for Evaluating Combinatorial Counting in Large Language Models
summary: We present CombEval, a dynamic benchmark for evaluating combinatorial counting in large language models. CombEval represents each problem as a typed Cofola specification over entities, combinatorial objects, object dependencies, and constraints, enabling controlled generation of natural-language counting problems with exact solver-verified answers. Unlike static collections, CombEval supports systematic variation of object type, entity scale, constraint count, and reasoning depth. We evaluate 11 LLMs under direct and code-augmented settings and find that models remain brittle on ordered objects, indistinguishable elements, relatively positional constraints, and nested object dependencies. Error analysis further identifies failures in constraint interpretation and counting principles. CombEval provides a diagnostic testbed for studying when and why LLMs fail at combinatorial reasoning. The code and generated benchmark suites are publicly available at \url{https://github.com/YuxuZhou-CN/combination-problem-generation}.

AI.tldr: CombEval is a dynamic benchmark for evaluating combinatorial counting in LLMs, using typed Cofola specifications to generate verifiable problems. Testing 11 LLMs reveals brittleness on ordered objects, indistinguishable elements, relative constraints, and nested dependencies, with errors in constraint interpretation and counting principles.
AI.motivation: Existing static benchmarks cannot systematically vary problem parameters (object type, entity scale, constraint count, reasoning depth) to diagnose LLM failures in combinatorial counting, motivating a dynamic, controllable benchmark.
AI.method: CombEval represents each problem as a typed Cofola specification over entities, combinatorial objects, object dependencies, and constraints, enabling controlled natural-language problem generation with exact solver-verified answers.
AI.result: 11 LLMs evaluated under direct and code-augmented settings; models are brittle on ordered objects, indistinguishable elements, relative positional constraints, and nested object dependencies. Error analysis identifies failures in constraint interpretation and counting principles.
AI.conclusion: CombEval serves as a diagnostic testbed for understanding when and why LLMs fail at combinatorial reasoning, with code and benchmark suites publicly released.

title: Co-policy: Responsive Human-Robot Co-Creation for Musical Performances
summary: Art has long stood as a pivotal expression of human creativity. Embodied artificial intelligence offers a route for generative models to participate in that creativity through physical action rather than disembodied digital content. In robotic music co-creation, it is challenging to connect semantic musical understanding with real-time and physically executable performance. We present Co-policy, a framework for human-robot musical co-creation that separates semantic intent grounding, constrained musical variation, and visuomotor execution. To ground musical semantics, Co-policy uses pre-inference semantic anchors and a fine-tuned Qwen-vl planner (F-Qwen) to transform speech, live musical seeds, and visual observations into structured co-creation plans. To support low-latency execution, Co-policy introduces a Gaussian-Mixture Visuomotor Policy (GMP), implemented as a conditional mixture-density policy that maps target notes and visual context to multimodal robot actions in a single forward pass. Unlike robotic playback systems that merely reproduce user-specified notes, Co-policy generates complementary musical responses under both musical and physical constraints. Real-robot chime experiments, ablations, and expert evaluation show improved intent alignment, execution accuracy, and response frequency over diffusion-policy and ablated baselines, supporting physically grounded action generation as a key requirement for embodied human-AI co-creation.

AI.tldr: Co-policy is a framework for human-robot musical co-creation that separates semantic intent grounding, constrained musical variation, and visuomotor execution, using a fine-tuned Qwen-vl planner and a Gaussian-Mixture Visuomotor Policy (GMP) to enable real-time, physically executable, complementary musical responses rather than mere playback.
AI.motivation: To enable embodied AI to participate in physical creative expression (robotic music co-creation) by bridging the gap between semantic musical understanding and real-time, physically executable robot performance.
AI.method: Co-policy uses a three-component pipeline: (1) semantic intent grounding via pre-inference semantic anchors and a fine-tuned Qwen-vl planner (F-Qwen) that processes speech, live musical seeds, and visual observations; (2) constrained musical variation; and (3) visuomotor execution via a Gaussian-Mixture Visuomotor Policy (GMP) — a conditional mixture-density policy that maps target notes and visual context to multimodal robot actions in a single forward pass for low latency.
AI.result: Real-robot chime experiments, ablations, and expert evaluation show improved intent alignment, execution accuracy, and response frequency over diffusion-policy and ablated baselines.
AI.conclusion: Physically grounded action generation is a key requirement for embodied human-AI co-creation, and Co-policy demonstrates a viable approach for robots to generate complementary, musically constrained responses in real-time physical interaction.

title: Think Again or Think Longer? Selective Verification for Budget-Aware Reasoning
summary: Test-time reasoning is increasingly used as a serving-time control knob, but extra reasoning is not uniformly valuable: it can repair failed attempts, waste compute on already-correct answers, or introduce harmful answer changes. We study this as a deployment allocation problem rather than a new-verifier problem. We introduce \sevra, Selective Verification for Reasoning Allocation, a serving-layer controller that decides whether to preserve a frozen solver's initial answer or invoke active verification. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B solver, we log intervention outcomes and train recoverability-aware gates from serving-visible attempt state. On \mathfive, selective verification reaches 76.3\% accuracy, compared with 75.5\% for always verifying, while reducing post-generation tokens by 26.8\% and harmful flips from 2.2\% to 1.0\%. However, an 8,192-token initial solve reaches 76.0\% accuracy with 28\% fewer total model tokens, showing that selective recovery is useful but not the best tested cost frontier. In frozen transfer to \gsm, the selective policy verifies only 3.0\% of examples, improves accuracy from 93.4\% to 94.5\%, and reduces verification tokens by 91.2\% relative to always verifying; again, a longer initial solve matches its accuracy with fewer realized tokens. On CommonsenseQA, always-on verification hurts, while Self-Consistency@5 improves accuracy at about five times the realized token cost. The resulting deployment rule is: tune the initial budget first, then use selective recovery when explicit checks, bounded retries, auditability, or regression-risk control matter.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SEVRA, a selective verification system that decides when to invoke active verification on a frozen solver's initial answer based on serving-visible attempt state, showing it reduces computational cost and harmful flips compared to always-verifying, but also finds that tuning the initial compute budget often achieves better cost-accuracy tradeoffs.
AI.motivation: Test-time reasoning is not uniformly valuable across examples—extra compute can repair failures, waste resources on already-correct answers, or introduce harmful answer changes. The authors frame this as a deployment allocation problem rather than building a new verifier.
AI.method: The authors propose SEVRA (Selective Verification for Reasoning Allocation), a serving-layer controller that uses a frozen Qwen3-4B solver and trains recoverability-aware gates from serving-visible attempt state to decide between preserving the initial answer or invoking active verification.
AI.result: On MATH-500, selective verification achieves 76.3% accuracy (vs 75.5% for always verifying), reduces post-generation tokens by 26.8% and harmful flips from 2.2% to 1.0%. However, an 8,192-token initial solve reaches 76.0% with 28% fewer total tokens. On GSM8K, selective policy verifies only 3% of examples, improves accuracy from 93.4% to 94.5%, and reduces verification tokens by 91.2%. On CommonsenseQA, always-on verification hurts.
AI.conclusion: The resulting deployment rule is: tune the initial compute budget first, then use selective recovery when explicit checks, bounded retries, auditability, or regression-risk control are needed. Selective verification is useful but not the best tested cost frontier compared to longer initial solves.

title: Deep-Unfolded Coordination
comment: The second and third authors contributed equally (equal second authorship). 35 pages (10 pages main text), 17 figures, 3 tables
summary: Distributed optimization is a highly scalable and structurally transparent technique to solve multi-agent robotics problems; however, such methods often suffer from the need for highly-specialized, problem-specific hyperparameter tunings. In this work, we propose Deep Coordinator, a deep-unfolding framework that learns to dynamically adjust the hyperparameters of ADMM-DDP, a popular distributed solver for robotics tasks, at solve-time in response to optimizer performance. Our architecture consists of unrolling a fixed number of ADMM-DDP iterations into a neural network with learnable functions between layers mapping the optimizer state to the next hyperparameters. To the best of our knowledge, Deep Coordinator is the first deep-unfolding framework to adapt the penalty parameters of a non-convex optimizer at solve-time; we show that the mainstream supervised approach can yield degenerate solutions when training such models, and propose an unsupervised learning scheme. On simulations with fleets of cars and quadrotors, Deep Coordinator produces trajectories of comparable quality 6.18-9.44x faster than conventional solvers. Furthermore, Deep Coordinator retains its performance benefits when deployed to systems up to 8x larger than trained on.

AI.tldr: Deep Coordinator is a deep-unfolding framework that learns to dynamically adjust ADMM-DDP hyperparameters at solve-time, achieving 6.18-9.44x speedup on multi-robot trajectory planning while generalizing to systems 8x larger than trained on.
AI.motivation: Distributed optimization methods for multi-agent robotics require highly-specialized, problem-specific hyperparameter tunings, limiting their practicality and scalability.
AI.method: Deep Coordinator unrolls a fixed number of ADMM-DDP iterations into a neural network with learnable functions between layers that map optimizer state to next hyperparameters; uses an unsupervised learning scheme to avoid degenerate solutions from supervised training.
AI.result: Produces trajectories of comparable quality 6.18-9.44x faster than conventional solvers; retains performance when deployed to systems up to 8x larger than trained on.
AI.conclusion: Deep Coordinator is the first deep-unfolding framework to adapt penalty parameters of a non-convex optimizer at solve-time, offering significant acceleration and strong generalization for distributed multi-robot optimization.

title: Human-on-the-Loop Orchestration for AI-Assisted Legal Discovery
summary: Autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in electronic discovery (e-discovery), where compounding errors across multi-step reasoning chains can constitute legal malpractice. Unlike single-turn retrieval, agentic workflows operating over privileged document corpora exhibit a class of failure we term "trajectory collapse": an early misclassification silently propagates, rendering an entire privilege review invalid. This paper makes three contributions. First, we propose a structured taxonomy of agentic failures in legal information retrieval, organized by functional stage. Second, we introduce a four-layer verification architecture -- spanning planning, reasoning, execution, and uncertainty quantification -- designed to intercept these failures before they compound. Third, we present a preliminary simulation study on a synthetic e-discovery corpus that demonstrates how mandatory Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL) escalation thresholds reduce privilege-waiver risk relative to fully autonomous baselines. Our results suggest that calibrated uncertainty thresholds can reduce privilege-waiver risk by up to 61% versus fully autonomous deployment, while routing fewer than one quarter of documents to attorney review.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies "trajectory collapse" failures in autonomous LLM agents used for e-discovery privilege review, proposes a taxonomy of agentic failures, introduces a four-layer verification architecture, and demonstrates through simulation that Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL) escalation with calibrated uncertainty thresholds can reduce privilege-waiver risk by up to 61% while requiring attorney review for fewer than 25% of documents.
AI.motivation: Autonomous LLM agents are increasingly used in e-discovery, but compounding errors across multi-step reasoning chains can lead to legal malpractice. The authors identify a specific failure mode called "trajectory collapse" where early misclassifications silently propagate, invalidating entire privilege reviews.
AI.method: The authors propose a structured taxonomy of agentic failures in legal information retrieval organized by functional stage, introduce a four-layer verification architecture covering planning, reasoning, execution, and uncertainty quantification, and conduct a preliminary simulation study on a synthetic e-discovery corpus comparing fully autonomous baselines with mandatory HOTL escalation thresholds.
AI.result: Calibrated uncertainty thresholds reduce privilege-waiver risk by up to 61% versus fully autonomous deployment, while routing fewer than one quarter of documents to attorney review.
AI.conclusion: Human-on-the-Loop escalation thresholds with calibrated uncertainty quantification effectively mitigate trajectory collapse risks in agentic legal workflows, balancing automation efficiency with risk reduction in high-stakes e-discovery contexts.

title: SWAP: Symmetric Equivariant World-Model for Agile Robot Parkour
summary: While latent world models enable the proactive predictions required for extreme parkour, their purely data-driven nature forces them to redundantly encode left-right symmetric interactions as independent patterns. This inflates the learning burden and hinders the capture of geometric regularities, restricting the latent space's efficiency for downstream policies. To address this, we propose SWAP, an end-to-end equivariant symmetric world model. This framework embeds symmetry directly into both the world model and the actor-critic networks. In real-world tests, the robot leaps across a 2.13 m gap and climbs a 1.63 m platform, breaking records for quadruped parkour. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robust geometric generalization to unseen mirrored terrains and exceptional zero-shot transferability across diverse outdoor environments. These results demonstrate that symmetry equivariance is an effective structural prior for pushing the physical boundaries of learned legged locomotion.

AI.tldr: SWAP is an end-to-end equivariant symmetric world model that embeds symmetry into world model and actor-critic networks for quadruped parkour, enabling a robot to leap across a 2.13m gap and climb a 1.63m platform, breaking records.
AI.motivation: Latent world models redundantly encode left-right symmetric interactions as independent patterns due to purely data-driven nature, inflating learning burden and hindering geometric regularity capture, restricting latent space efficiency for downstream policies.
AI.method: Proposes SWAP, an end-to-end equivariant symmetric world model that embeds symmetry directly into both the world model and actor-critic networks.
AI.result: Robot leaps across 2.13m gap and climbs 1.63m platform, breaking quadruped parkour records; exhibits robust geometric generalization to unseen mirrored terrains and exceptional zero-shot transferability across diverse outdoor environments.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry equivariance is an effective structural prior for pushing physical boundaries of learned legged locomotion.

authors: V V N K Someswara Rao Koduri
title: TelcoAgent: A Scalable 5G Multi-KPM Forecasting With 3GPP-Grounded Explainability
comment: 6 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE GLOBECOM 2026
summary: Key Performance Measurement (KPM) forecasting is essential for proactive network management of 5G and next-generation telecom networks. However, existing machine learning (ML) approaches face significant limitations in scalability and explainability, restricting their effectiveness in real-world deployments. We propose TelcoAgent, a foundation model-based framework that enables accurate, scalable, and explainable forecasting of multiple KPMs across diverse network cells without the need for site-specific training. Specifically, the framework comprises three key components: (i) an automated three-agent pipeline that constructs a 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) knowledge graph directly from specification documents, (ii) a scalable, time-series foundation model (TSFM)-based prediction pipeline to deliver accurate, zero-shot forecasting, and finally (iii) a reasoning and explanation pipeline that provides actionable, domain-grounded diagnostics. Evaluated using a 3-month, real-world, city-scale 5G KPM dataset from a U.S.-based network operator, TelcoAgent demonstrates high forecasting accuracy for all 7 considered KPMs per cell across 200 cells, while delivering explainable insights and actionable instructions to address network degradations.

AI.tldr: TelcoAgent is a foundation model-based framework for accurate, scalable, and explainable 5G Key Performance Measurement forecasting across multiple cells without site-specific training, using a 3GPP knowledge graph, time-series foundation model prediction, and reasoning pipeline for actionable diagnostics.
AI.motivation: Existing ML approaches for KPM forecasting in 5G/next-gen networks suffer from scalability and explainability limitations, hindering real-world deployment effectiveness.
AI.method: TelcoAgent consists of three components: (i) an automated three-agent pipeline constructing a 3GPP knowledge graph from specification documents, (ii) a TSFM-based zero-shot prediction pipeline, and (iii) a reasoning and explanation pipeline providing domain-grounded diagnostics.
AI.result: Evaluated on a 3-month, real-world, city-scale 5G KPM dataset from a U.S. operator, achieving high forecasting accuracy for all 7 KPMs across 200 cells with explainable insights and actionable instructions.
AI.conclusion: TelcoAgent enables accurate, scalable, and explainable multi-KPM forecasting without site-specific training, addressing key limitations of prior ML approaches for real-world telecom network management.

title: Motor Angular Speed Preintegration for Multirotor UAV State Estimation
summary: A precise state estimate is crucial for a tight feedback control that enables agile and near-obstacle flights of UAVs. The state-of-the-art methods fuse slow pose measurements with high-frequency inertial measurements to obtain a precise state estimate. However, the inertial measurements from the IMU onboard the UAV are degraded by vibrations from spinning propellers and the precision of the estimated state suffers. We propose a novel approach based on the preintegration of accelerations obtained from motor speeds. We show that the accelerations obtained in this manner can be used for state propagation on their own to achieve better precision without including the IMU. Further, we propose a factor composed of the preintegrated motor speeds that can be directly employed in factor graph optimization frameworks. We combine our factor with LiDAR measurements into the proposed Motor Angular Speed LiDAR Odometry (MAS-LO) algorithm for precise state estimation, which we open-source. Lastly, we evaluate the estimation precision against a state-of-the-art inertial algorithm LIO-SAM to show 28% improvement in position and 65% in velocity estimation accuracy, 14% lower measurement lag, and high robustness to wrong parameter values.

AI.tldr: MAS-LO replaces traditional IMU-based state propagation with preintegrated motor speed accelerations, achieving 28% better position and 65% better velocity accuracy than LIO-SAM, with lower latency and higher robustness to parameter errors.
AI.motivation: IMU measurements on UAVs are degraded by propeller-induced vibrations, reducing state estimation precision. Existing fusion methods suffer from this noise source, motivating the need for an alternative inertial source.
AI.method: Preintegrate accelerations derived from motor speeds (instead of IMU) for state propagation; formulate a factor graph optimization factor from preintegrated motor speeds; combine with LiDAR measurements in the MAS-LO algorithm.
AI.result: 28% improvement in position accuracy, 65% improvement in velocity accuracy, 14% lower measurement lag, and high robustness to wrong parameter values compared to LIO-SAM.
AI.conclusion: Motor-speed-derived accelerations are a viable and superior alternative to IMU measurements for state estimation in UAVs, particularly under vibration-heavy operating conditions.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Black-Box Uncertainty Estimation Methods for Large Language Models
summary: Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities across a wide range of tasks, their outputs often remain unreliable and may contain hallucinations, making uncertainty estimation (UE) essential for building trustworthy LLMs. In practice, many mainstream LLMs are only accessible through restricted APIs, where internal signals such as logits and hidden states are unavailable, making black-box UE especially important. However, existing work on black-box UE for LLMs remains fragmented in methodology and lacks a unified empirical comparison. To address this gap, we present a systematic review of black-box UE methods and organize them into five categories: verbalization-based, sampling-based, explanation-based, multi-agent, and hybrid methods. We further build a unified evaluation framework and benchmark 24 representative methods across 4 models and 4 dataset settings. Our results show that no single method consistently dominates across all settings. Nevertheless, methods that reason over and compare candidates in the answer space are generally effective, and hybrid methods that combine multiple uncertainty signals perform well under most conditions. By releasing the benchmark data and a unified evaluation framework, we aim to facilitate reproducible comparisons and support future research, while our empirical findings provide practical guidance for developing future black-box UE methods for LLMs.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a systematic review and unified empirical benchmark of black-box uncertainty estimation (UE) methods for LLMs, categorizing 24 methods into 5 types (verbalization-based, sampling-based, explanation-based, multi-agent, hybrid) and evaluating them across 4 models and 4 datasets. No single method dominates all settings, but answer-space reasoning methods and hybrid approaches generally perform well.
AI.motivation: LLM outputs are often unreliable and contain hallucinations, making uncertainty estimation essential for trustworthy systems. Many mainstream LLMs are only accessible via restricted APIs (no logits/hidden states), making black-box UE crucial. However, existing work on black-box UE is fragmented methodologically and lacks unified empirical comparison.
AI.method: The authors conduct a systematic literature review, organizing black-box UE methods into five categories: verbalization-based, sampling-based, explanation-based, multi-agent, and hybrid methods. They build a unified evaluation framework and benchmark 24 representative methods across 4 LLMs and 4 dataset settings.
AI.result: No single method consistently dominates across all settings. Methods that reason over and compare candidates in the answer space are generally effective. Hybrid methods combining multiple uncertainty signals perform well under most conditions.
AI.conclusion: The authors release benchmark data and a unified evaluation framework to facilitate reproducible comparisons. Their empirical findings provide practical guidance for developing future black-box UE methods for LLMs.

title: Evaluation of Augmented Reality-based Intuitive Interface for Robot-Assisted Transesophageal Echocardiography: A User Study
summary: TransEsophageal Echocardiography (TEE) is essential for diagnosing and guiding Structural Heart Disease (SHD) interventions. However, manual TEE manipulation demands significant operator expertise, is physically demanding, and exposes clinicians to radiation when performed alongside fluoroscopy. Robotic-assisted TEE systems have been introduced to improve probe handling and reduce operator fatigue, yet the design of intuitive and effective user interfaces remains an open challenge. This study presents and evaluates a model-enhanced, Augmented Reality (AR)-based intuitive interface for robot-assisted TEE, designed to improve spatial awareness and control intuitiveness. A robotic TEE platform integrated with electromagnetic tracking and a virtual simulator was used to compare three user interfaces differing in visualization and interaction modalities: 2D jointlevel (2D-JI), 3D joint-level (3D-JI), and 3D tip-level (3D-TI). Thirty six participants performed standardized navigation tasks to reproduce target echocardiographic views, with performance assessed via position and orientation errors, completion time, and NASA-TLX workload scores. Results show that 3D visualization significantly improved spatial accuracy, reducing median position error from 13 mm to 3 mm and halving the orientation error compared with the 2D interface. Tip-level interaction yielded a further 50% reduction in orientation error and reduced interuser variability relative to joint-level control. Overall, the 3D-TI configuration, combining immersive visualization with direct tip-level control, proved the most effective and ergonomic interface, supporting the integration of AR-based visualization and intuitive control paradigms into next-generation robotic TEE systems to enhance operator performance and procedural safety.

AI.tldr: This study presents and evaluates a model-enhanced Augmented Reality (AR)-based intuitive interface for robot-assisted TransEsophageal Echocardiography (TEE). Three interfaces (2D joint-level, 3D joint-level, 3D tip-level) were compared across 36 participants. The 3D tip-level configuration significantly improved spatial accuracy (position error reduced from 13mm to 3mm), halved orientation error, and reduced workload, proving the most effective and ergonomic interface for robotic TEE systems.
AI.motivation: Manual TEE manipulation requires significant operator expertise, is physically demanding, and exposes clinicians to radiation when combined with fluoroscopy. While robotic-assisted TEE systems exist, designing intuitive and effective user interfaces remains an open challenge.
AI.method: A robotic TEE platform with electromagnetic tracking and virtual simulator was used. Three interfaces were compared: 2D joint-level (2D-JI), 3D joint-level (3D-JI), and 3D tip-level (3D-TI). Thirty-six participants performed standardized navigation tasks to reproduce target echocardiographic views. Performance was assessed via position/orientation errors, completion time, and NASA-TLX workload scores.
AI.result: 3D visualization significantly improved spatial accuracy, reducing median position error from 13 mm to 3 mm and halving orientation error compared to 2D interface. Tip-level interaction yielded a further 50% reduction in orientation error and reduced inter-user variability relative to joint-level control. The 3D-TI configuration was the most effective and ergonomic interface.
AI.conclusion: The 3D-TI configuration, combining immersive AR visualization with direct tip-level control, proved most effective. The findings support integrating AR-based visualization and intuitive control paradigms into next-generation robotic TEE systems to enhance operator performance and procedural safety.

title: MetaResearcher: Scaling Deep Research via Self-Reflective Reinforcement Learning in Adversarial Virtual Environments
summary: Deep research agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in autonomous information gathering and synthesis, yet their training remains constrained by the static nature of simulated environments, the limits of fact-retrieval-only task designs, and the inefficiency of outcome-based reinforcement learning. In this work, we propose MetaResearcher, a novel framework that scales deep research agent training across four synergistic dimensions. First, we introduce an Evolving Virtual World that injects temporal dynamics and adversarial misinformation into the training environment, forcing agents to develop source credibility assessment and temporal conflict resolution skills. Second, we design Discovery-Oriented Tasks -- including hypothesis generation and contradiction resolution -- that transcend simple fact retrieval and push agents toward genuine research behaviors. Third, we propose a Self-Reflective Meta-Reward mechanism within the GRPO framework that jointly optimizes for answer correctness, search path efficiency, reflection depth, and tool call diversity, directly addressing the repetitive action loop problem observed in prior work. Fourth, we introduce a Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Swarm architecture comprising specialized Scout, Filter, and Synthesizer models that learn collaborative research strategies through coordinated reinforcement learning. Built upon the LiteResearcher infrastructure, MetaResearcher requires zero marginal API cost for training while targeting substantial improvements in both benchmark performance (GAIA, Xbench-DS) and epistemic robustness under adversarial conditions. We present the complete framework design, training methodology, and planned experimental validation.

AI.tldr: MetaResearcher is a framework that scales deep research agent training across four dimensions: an Evolving Virtual World with temporal dynamics and misinformation, Discovery-Oriented Tasks beyond fact retrieval, a Self-Reflective Meta-Reward mechanism in GRPO, and a Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Swarm architecture, all built on LiteResearcher with zero marginal API cost.
AI.motivation: Current deep research agents are limited by static simulated environments, fact-retrieval-only task designs, and inefficient outcome-based reinforcement learning, necessitating more dynamic and comprehensive training approaches.
AI.method: Four synergistic training dimensions: (1) Evolving Virtual World with temporal dynamics and adversarial misinformation, (2) Discovery-Oriented Tasks including hypothesis generation and contradiction resolution, (3) Self-Reflective Meta-Reward mechanism within GRPO optimizing correctness, efficiency, reflection depth, and tool diversity, (4) Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Swarm with specialized Scout, Filter, and Synthesizer models using coordinated RL.
AI.result: Zero marginal API cost for training; targets substantial improvements on GAIA and Xbench-DS benchmarks and epistemic robustness under adversarial conditions.
AI.conclusion: MetaResearcher provides a comprehensive framework for training more capable and robust deep research agents through multi-dimensional scaling of environment dynamics, task diversity, reward design, and multi-agent coordination.

title: Tri-Info: Generalizable, Interpretable Failure Prediction for VLA Models via Information Theory
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are increasingly deployed across diverse tasks, yet they remain black boxes whose physical interactions can cause irreversible harm, making generalizable and interpretable failure detection essential. We observe that successful and failed rollouts carry systematically different information-theoretic signatures. Building on this, we formalize VLA control as a closed-loop information pipeline and derive the Triple Information-theoretic (Tri-Info) signals that capture whether actions remain diverse, temporally consistent, and coupled to state transitions. Across six VLA models and three benchmark environments, Tri-Info matches the strongest baselines in-domain. Moreover, Tri-Info transfers across architectures, environments, and the sim-to-real gap without retraining, reaching 83\% accuracy on real-world tasks where prior detectors collapse to chance. This establishes Tri-Info as a simple yet powerful method that not only detects failures with strong cross-domain generalization, but also delivers interpretable diagnostics of the underlying failure modes.

AI.tldr: Tri-Info is a method that extracts three information-theoretic signals from VLA models—action diversity, temporal consistency, and state-action coupling—to detect execution failures. It matches strong baselines in-domain and generalizes across architectures, environments, and sim-to-real gaps without retraining, achieving 83% accuracy on real-world tasks where prior methods fail.
AI.motivation: VLA models are black boxes whose failures during physical interaction can cause irreversible harm, necessitating generalizable and interpretable failure detection methods.
AI.method: Formalizes VLA control as a closed-loop information pipeline and derives Triple Information-theoretic (Tri-Info) signals: action diversity, temporal consistency, and coupling between actions and state transitions.
AI.result: Matches strongest baselines in-domain; transfers across architectures, environments, and sim-to-real gap without retraining; achieves 83% accuracy on real-world tasks where prior detectors collapse to chance.
AI.conclusion: Tri-Info is a simple, powerful, and interpretable failure detection method with strong cross-domain generalization, providing diagnostics of underlying failure modes.

title: Multi-Agent Transactive Memory
summary: The decentralized deployment of LLM agents with diverse capabilities across diverse tasks motivates infrastructure for knowledge sharing across heterogeneous agent populations. Just as search engines index human-generated artifacts to support human problem solving, retrieval systems can organize agent-generated artifacts for reuse across agent populations. We extend retrieval-augmented generation - which demonstrates the value of human-authored artifacts to individual agents - to retrieval of agent-generated artifacts supporting a population of agents. In particular, agent trajectories encode reusable procedural knowledge, yet these artifacts are typically discarded after a single use or retained only by the producing agent, forcing newly instantiated agents to repeatedly rediscover existing solutions. We propose Multi-Agent Transactive Memory (MATM), a framework for population-level storage and retrieval of agent-generated trajectories, where producer agents contribute trajectories to a shared repository and consumer agents retrieve them to improve task execution. We focus on interactive environments (ALFWorld and WebArena), where trajectories are long and encode especially rich procedural structure. Our experiments demonstrate that retrieving trajectories from MATM improves downstream task performance and reduces interaction steps without coordination or joint training. These results position MATM as a design pattern for population-level experience sharing in open agent ecosystems.

AI.tldr: MATM is a framework for population-level storage and retrieval of LLM agent trajectories across heterogeneous agents, enabling knowledge sharing without coordination or joint training, improving task performance in interactive environments like ALFWorld and WebArena.
AI.motivation: Agent-generated trajectories encode reusable procedural knowledge but are typically discarded after a single use or retained only by the producing agent, forcing newly instantiated agents to repeatedly rediscover existing solutions. This motivates infrastructure for knowledge sharing across heterogeneous agent populations.
AI.method: Multi-Agent Transactive Memory (MATM) extends retrieval-augmented generation to agent-generated artifacts. Producer agents contribute trajectories to a shared repository; consumer agents retrieve them to improve task execution in interactive environments (ALFWorld and WebArena).
AI.result: Retrieving trajectories from MATM improves downstream task performance and reduces interaction steps without requiring coordination or joint training.
AI.conclusion: MATM serves as a design pattern for population-level experience sharing in open agent ecosystems, analogous to how search engines index human artifacts for human problem solving.

title: A Neuromorphic Reinforcement Learning Framework for Efficient Pathfinding in Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems
summary: Dynamic environmental changes, confined workspaces, and stringent real-time constraints make pathfinding in Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems (RMFS) a challenging problem for conventional search- and rule-based methods, which typically suffer from high computational complexity and long decision latency. While reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful alternative, deploying learned policies with extreme energy efficiency on resource-constrained hardware remains an open challenge. We present SDQN-RMFS, an end-to-end framework that achieves high-fidelity deployment of an RL-trained policy from a full-precision artificial neural network (ANN) through to a neuromorphic chip. By computing only when triggered by sparse events, this framework unlocks ultra-low-power RMFS pathfinding. Our full-stack pipeline operates as follows: an ANN policy is first efficiently trained via a collision-allowing strategy to densify informative trajectories, and then converted into a spiking neural network (SNN) via a hard-label knowledge distillation approach. This effectively addresses the output distribution mismatch, preserving policy capability across the ANN-to-SNN pipeline while substantially reducing inference latency. Hardware experiments demonstrate up to 11,281$\times$ energy savings and a nearly two-fold reduction in latency compared to a high-performance GPU baseline, while maintaining decision quality on par with the original trained policy. These results establish physical neuromorphic inference as a practical and energy-sustainable pathway for large-scale RMFS operations.

AI.tldr: SDQN-RMFS is an end-to-end framework that deploys RL-trained policies from full-precision ANNs to neuromorphic chips for ultra-low-power RMFS pathfinding, achieving up to 11,281× energy savings and near 2× latency reduction vs GPU baselines while maintaining policy quality.
AI.motivation: Pathfinding in RMFS faces challenges from dynamic environments, confined spaces, and real-time constraints; conventional methods suffer high complexity and latency, while deploying RL policies on resource-constrained hardware with extreme energy efficiency remains an open challenge.
AI.method: The full-stack pipeline: (1) ANN policy trained with a collision-allowing strategy to densify informative trajectories; (2) ANN is converted to a spiking neural network (SNN) via hard-label knowledge distillation to address output distribution mismatch and preserve policy capability; (3) SNN is deployed on a neuromorphic chip for event-driven, ultra-low-power inference.
AI.result: Up to 11,281× energy savings and nearly 2× latency reduction compared to a high-performance GPU baseline, while decision quality remains on par with the original trained policy.
AI.conclusion: Physical neuromorphic inference is established as a practical and energy-sustainable pathway for large-scale RMFS operations.

title: eCNNTO: A Highly Generalizable ConvNet for Accelerating Topology Optimization
summary: This work proposes an element-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to accelerate density-based Topology Optimization (TO), termed eCNNTO. TO generally undergoes a large number of iterations, where finite element analysis is performed in every iteration, leading to the efficiency bottleneck especially when dense meshes are used to achieve high-resolution designs. To address this limitation, eCNNTO is proposed to build upon Kallioras et al. (2020), where a Deep Belief Network (DBN) was trained for every element to predict its near-optimal density from its early history, thereby skipping the great majority of iterations and significantly accelerating the TO procedure. However, the method lacks spatial correlations among neighboring elements and may lead to disconnected features in the final structure. The proposed method employs CNN with residual connections to address this issue. On top of it, a novel training strategy is introduced to further enhance the optimization efficiency, where the training dataset consists of the final stage density histories rather than early ones. This change can also help reduce the required training data size. eCNNTO requires only a small dataset to train and yet it can be generalized to problems with largely different boundary conditions, loading cases, design domain geometries, mesh resolutions, as well as non-design domains. In the end, the generalization capabilities and efficiency of eCNNTO are demonstrated through a variety of examples in two and three dimensions, achieving up to 90% and 97% reduction of iterations, respectively.

AI.tldr: eCNNTO uses a CNN with residual connections to predict near-optimal element densities from early history, accelerating topology optimization by up to 97% while maintaining spatial coherence across elements, requiring only small training datasets and generalizing to diverse problem settings.
AI.motivation: Traditional density-based Topology Optimization (TO) requires many iterations with costly finite element analysis per iteration, creating an efficiency bottleneck especially for high-resolution designs. Prior work using Deep Belief Networks (DBN) per element lacks spatial correlations, leading to disconnected structural features.
AI.method: The method replaces element-wise DBNs with a CNN featuring residual connections to capture spatial correlations between neighboring elements. A novel training strategy uses density histories from the final optimization stage (rather than early stage) to build the training dataset, reducing required data size and improving efficiency.
AI.result: Achieves up to 90% iteration reduction in 2D and 97% in 3D problems. Generalizes well across different boundary conditions, loading cases, geometries, mesh resolutions, and non-design domains, all with small training datasets.
AI.conclusion: eCNNTO effectively accelerates TO while preserving structural connectivity through CNN-based spatial modeling, demonstrating strong generalization and data efficiency for practical high-resolution topology optimization.

title: MirrorDuo: Reflection-Consistent Visuomotor Learning from Mirrored Demonstration Pairs
summary: Image-based behaviour cloning leverages demonstrations captured from ubiquitous RGB cameras. However, it remains constrained by the cost of collecting diverse demos, especially for generalizing across workspace variations. We propose MirrorDuo, a reflection-based formulation that operates on image, proprioception, and full 6-DoF end-effector action tuples, generating a mirrored counterpart for each original demonstration, effectively achieving "collect one, get one for free". It can be applied as a data augmentation strategy for existing learning pipelines, such as standard behaviour cloning or diffusion policy, or as a structural prior for reflection-equivariant policy networks. By leveraging the overlap between the original and mirrored domains, MirrorDuo achieves significantly improved performance under the same data budget when demonstrations are evenly distributed across both sides of the workspace. When demonstrations are confined to one side, MirrorDuo enables efficient skill transfer to the mirrored workspace with as few as zero or five demos in the target arrangement.

AI.tldr: MirrorDuo is a reflection-based data augmentation method that creates mirrored versions of robot manipulation demonstrations from RGB cameras, doubling the effective data at no extra cost. It improves behaviour cloning performance under limited data budgets and enables zero/few-shot skill transfer across workspace sides.
AI.motivation: Image-based behaviour cloning is limited by the high cost of collecting diverse demonstrations, especially for generalizing across workspace variations (e.g., different sides of the workspace).
AI.method: MirrorDuo operates on (image, proprioception, 6-DoF end-effector action) tuples, generating a mirrored counterpart for each original demonstration via reflection transformations. It can be used as a data augmentation strategy for standard behaviour cloning/diffusion policy, or as a structural prior for reflection-equivariant policy networks.
AI.result: Significantly improved performance under the same data budget when demonstrations are evenly distributed across both workspace sides; enables efficient skill transfer to the mirrored workspace with as few as 0–5 demos when demonstrations are confined to one side.
AI.conclusion: MirrorDuo effectively achieves "collect one, get one for free", doubling demonstration data and enabling cross-workspace generalization with minimal additional data collection cost.

title: The Tao of Agency: Autotelic AI, Embedded Agency and Dissolution of the Self
summary:
Most artificial intelligence systems are built on the assumption that goals are exogenous and specified by the designer. Exploring what happens when an agent begins generating its own goals opens the field of autotelic AI. Agents are expected not merely to pursue objectives but to discover them. In this article, we trace its consequences through intrinsic motivation, resource-driven priors, causal-interventional learning, homeostasis, and embeddedness; the last of which is found to be a necessary but not sufficient condition for autotelic agency. Embeddedness individuates the agent at the cost of revealing that the individuation is non-unique, such that the same dynamics admit many valid partitions, each defining a different candidate self.
  The deepest problem with autotelic AI is therefore not how the agent generates goals, but how it generates and relativizes the self to which the goals are assigned. The agent must believe in its own boundary in order to act, and see through that boundary in order to understand. We consolidate these developments into a single framework and extend it along three directions: a quantum formulation in which the agent-environment cut becomes physical, a philosophical reading against non-dual contemplative traditions, and a concrete LLM-based agentic instantiation.

AI.tldr: This paper explores autotelic AI—agents that generate their own goals—tracing its foundations through intrinsic motivation, homeostasis, and embeddedness. It argues the core problem is not goal generation but self-generation: how an agent constructs and relativizes the self to which goals are assigned. The framework is extended into quantum formulations, non-dual philosophy, and LLM-based implementations.
AI.motivation: To shift AI from exogenous, designer-specified goals to autotelic systems where agents discover and generate their own goals, and to identify the fundamental challenge this poses: the problem of self-individuation.
AI.method: Conceptual synthesis: traces autotelic AI through intrinsic motivation, resource-driven priors, causal-interventional learning, homeostasis, and embeddedness. Extends the framework along three directions—quantum physics (agent-environment cut), non-dual contemplative philosophy, and concrete LLM-based instantiation.
AI.result: Identifies that embeddedness is necessary but insufficient for autotelic agency, and that self-individuation is non-unique. The deepest problem is not goal generation but how the agent generates and relativizes the self to which goals are assigned.
AI.conclusion: An autotelic agent must believe in its own boundary to act and see through that boundary to understand. The paper offers a unified framework and three extensions (quantum, philosophical, LLM-based) to address this paradox.

title: VFILC: Accurate Frequency Extrapolations in Imitation Learning via Sampling Frequency ILC
summary: Conventional neural network (NN)-based imitation learning methods for variable-speed motion either restricted their scope to interpolated speeds, or generated unpredictable motions when extrapolating beyond trained velocity ranges. Variable-frequency imitation learning (VFIL) enabled extrapolations of speeds by linking the NN model's sampling frequency to the motion frequency, whereas its open-loop configuration caused frequency errors, especially in the extrapolated high-frequency settings. This study proposes variable-frequency imitation learning with iterative learning control (VFILC) based on a combination of VFIL and iterative learning control (ILC) with both feedforward and feedback parts, the former taking advantage of VFIL and the latter adjusting the frequency errors. The experimental results showed that the proposed method successfully and accurately extrapolated motion speeds and reduced frequency errors in all three tasks, and that the feedback especially reduced the frequency errors by a remarkable 81% in the wiping task and 50% in the shaking task, both compared to simple feedforward VFIL, when extrapolating at double the average speed in the training data. The proposed method also improved accuracy by 27% compared with VFIL even at an interpolated frequency for a contact-rich mixing task affected by complex friction traits.

AI.tldr: Variable-Frequency Imitation Learning with Iterative Learning Control (VFILC) combines feedforward VFIL and feedback ILC to enable accurate extrapolation of motion speeds and reduce frequency errors in variable-speed imitation learning tasks.
AI.motivation: Conventional NN-based imitation learning for variable-speed motion struggles with speed extrapolation (unpredictable motions) and VFIL's open-loop configuration causes frequency errors, especially in high-frequency extrapolation settings.
AI.method: VFILC combines VFIL (feedforward) with ILC (feedback) to jointly model motion frequency and correct frequency errors via iterative learning control.
AI.result: VFILC successfully extrapolated motion speeds and reduced frequency errors across all three tasks; feedback reduced frequency errors by 81% (wiping) and 50% (shaking) at double average training speed, and improved accuracy by 27% over VFIL in a contact-rich mixing task.
AI.conclusion: The proposed VFILC method enables accurate and reliable speed extrapolation in imitation learning by integrating feedback-based frequency correction, outperforming open-loop VFIL in both interpolated and extrapolated regimes.

title: PhysDrift: Bridging the Embodiment Gap in Humanoid Co-Speech Motion Generation
summary: Humanoid robots require co-speech motions that are not only expressive and speech-aligned, but also physically executable under embodiment constraints. Existing co-speech generation pipelines are predominantly human-centric: motions are first generated in human-body representations such as SMPL-X and subsequently retargeted to humanoid robots. In this work, we identify a fundamental embodiment gap in this paradigm, where the mismatch between human motion manifolds and humanoid embodiment constraints disrupts embodiment consistency during motion transfer and physical execution. Through extensive analysis, we show that although retargeting can preserve coarse motion semantics, it significantly compresses motion diversity and weakens prosody-motion synchronization, limiting expressive humanoid behaviors. To address this problem, we first propose IK-EER, a prosody-preserving humanoid motion curation framework that jointly optimizes kinematic feasibility and speech-motion temporal alignment during retargeting. Building upon the curated robot-native motion dataset, we further introduce PhysDrift, an embodiment-aware co-speech motion generation framework that directly predicts executable humanoid joint trajectories from speech without relying on intermediate human-body representations. Unlike conventional human-centric pipelines, PhysDrift maintains embodiment consistency throughout both training and inference while incorporating physical regularization to stabilize robot motion dynamics. Extensive experiments and real-world humanoid deployment demonstrate that embodiment-aware robot-native generation substantially improves speech-motion alignment, physical plausibility, motion smoothness, inference efficiency, and real-time interaction capability.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies an embodiment gap in human-to-humanoid co-speech motion retargeting, proposes IK-EER for prosody-preserving motion curation and PhysDrift for embodiment-aware direct robot-native motion generation, achieving improved speech-motion alignment, physical plausibility, and efficiency in real-world humanoid deployment.
AI.motivation: Existing co-speech generation pipelines are human-centric (generating motions in SMPL-X then retargeting to robots), but there is a fundamental embodiment gap where mismatch between human motion manifolds and humanoid embodiment constraints disrupts consistency, compresses motion diversity, and weakens prosody-motion synchronization, limiting expressive humanoid behaviors.
AI.method: First, IK-EER (Inverse Kinematics with Embodiment-aware prosody pReservation) is proposed as a curation framework that jointly optimizes kinematic feasibility and speech-motion temporal alignment during retargeting. Then, PhysDrift is introduced as an embodiment-aware co-speech generation framework that directly predicts executable humanoid joint trajectories from speech, bypassing intermediate human-body representations, and incorporates physical regularization to stabilize robot motion dynamics.
AI.result: Extensive experiments and real-world humanoid deployment show that embodiment-aware robot-native generation (PhysDrift) substantially improves speech-motion alignment, physical plausibility, motion smoothness, inference efficiency, and real-time interaction capability compared to human-centric pipelines.
AI.conclusion: Embodiment-aware robot-native generation outperforms conventional human-centric co-speech pipelines for humanoid robots, addressing the embodiment gap and enabling more expressive, physically feasible, and efficient co-speech motions.

title: Pose6DAug: Physically Plausible Multi-view Object Swapping for Robot Data Augmentation
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have shown strong potential for general-purpose manipulation, yet they often fail on novel, out-of-distribution objects whose appearance or geometry deviates from the training distribution. The standard remedy is to collect multi-view teleoperation data for every failure case, but this scales poorly in both cost and time. We introduce Pose6DAug, a failure-driven data augmentation framework that turns a policy's own successful episodes into targeted demonstrations for its failure modes, without any new data collection. Our key insight is that each successful episode already encodes a physically valid action trajectory together with calibrated multi-view observations. By swapping only the manipulated object while preserving this trajectory, we obtain new and physically grounded demonstrations. However, naive 2D video editing breaks multi-view consistency and physical plausibility, particularly under heavy occlusion and egocentric viewpoints. Our method instead operates directly in 3D, anchoring the target object with an explicit mesh driven by a temporally coherent 6D pose trajectory, ensuring geometrically consistent renderings across all camera views. Fine-tuning a VLA on data augmented by our method improves success rates by 16.5% relative to the state-of-the-art baseline on novel objects, while preserving in-distribution performance. These results show that multi-view and physically consistent augmentation is a practical path to scalable VLA generalization.

AI.tldr: Pose6DAug is a failure-driven data augmentation framework that repurposes a VLA policy's own successful episodes into training data for its failure cases by swapping manipulated objects with 3D-consistent mesh renderings guided by temporally coherent 6D pose trajectories, improving novel object generalization by 16.5% without new data collection.
AI.motivation: VLA policies struggle with novel, out-of-distribution objects due to appearance/geometry mismatch, and the standard remedy (collecting multi-view teleoperation data for each failure case) scales poorly in cost and time.
AI.method: Pose6DAug operates in 3D: it anchors the target object with an explicit mesh driven by a temporally coherent 6D pose trajectory, ensuring geometrically consistent renderings across all camera views. This allows swapping only the manipulated object while preserving the physically valid action trajectory from successful episodes.
AI.result: Fine-tuning on Pose6DAug-augmented data improves success rates by 16.5% relative to the state-of-the-art baseline on novel objects while preserving in-distribution performance.
AI.conclusion: Multi-view and physically consistent augmentation is a practical path to scalable VLA generalization without requiring additional data collection.

title: Advancing DialNav through Automatic Embodied Dialog Augmentation
summary: For embodied agents capable of physical interaction, the capability to create and understand dialog is crucial to ensure both safety and effectiveness. While DialNav~\cite{han2025dialnav} provides a framework for holistic evaluation of the dialog--execution loop in photorealistic indoor navigation, its performance remains limited by a critical scarcity of training data (2K episodes). To address this, we propose an automatic generation pipeline, and construct the \textbf{RAINbow} dataset, a large-scale training dataset with 238K episodes for DialNav. Our pipeline converts existing VLN datasets into multi-turn dialog and creates cost-efficient and high-quality dataset. Then, we introduce two additional complementary advances to unlock the data's full potential: (1) Dual-Strategy Training, a navigation training scheme to align the navigation training with the dynamic dialog-navigation loop, and (2) a localization model that leverages VLN knowledge. By combining these complementary solutions, our model substantially outperforms the baseline in success rate on both \textbf{Val Seen} (58.24, \textbf{+89\%}) and \textbf{Val Unseen} (29.05, \textbf{+100\%}) splits, establishing a new state of the art.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces RAINbow, a large-scale dataset (238K episodes) for DialNav, created via an automatic pipeline converting VLN datasets into multi-turn dialog. Combined with Dual-Strategy Training and a VLN knowledge-based localization model, it achieves +89-100% SOTA gains in navigation success rate.
AI.motivation: DialNav's performance is limited by critical data scarcity (only 2K episodes). The paper aims to address this bottleneck by generating a large-scale training dataset automatically.
AI.method: (1) An automatic generation pipeline converting existing VLN datasets into multi-turn dialog to create RAINbow (238K episodes). (2) Dual-Strategy Training to align navigation training with the dynamic dialog-navigation loop. (3) A localization model that leverages VLN knowledge.
AI.result: Substantially outperforms baseline on Val Seen (58.24, +89%) and Val Unseen (29.05, +100%), establishing new SOTA.
AI.conclusion: The complementary solutions (large-scale data + dual-strategy training + VLN-aware localization) effectively unlock the full potential of dialog-guided navigation for embodied agents.

title: Dual-Agent Framework for Cross-Model Verified Translation of Natural-Language Protocols into Robotic Laboratory Platform
summary: Biological experiment protocols are written in natural language, whereas automation systems rely on predefined control commands, creating a semantic gap that limits autonomous execution. Microplate-based automatic experiments are particularly challenging due to the need to simultaneously control well mapping, sample-reagent combinations, replicate placement, and parallel dispensing. This study proposes an agent-based protocol translation framework that converts natural-language microplate-based protocols into executable control commands for a robotic laboratory platform. A Parser Agent formalizes the natural-language protocol into a structured representation, and a rule-based mapping engine deterministically incorporates the operational constraints of the robotic laboratory platform to generate device-level control commands.
